# Credalti letter library — attorney review packet

<!-- Generated by `npm run letters:packet` from src/lib/letters. Do not edit by hand: change the templates or the catalogue and run the script again. -->

**Status: drafts pending attorney review.**

### What this is

This packet contains all 42 letter templates in the Credalti letter library. Every one is a DRAFT pending attorney review; each is marked "attorney_pending" in the software. 10 of them, marked "Original letter, in use today (wording unchanged)", are the letters the software already sends. The rest are new and are not used anywhere yet.

Each letter is written in the consumer's own name and over the consumer's own signature, and no letter mentions Credalti. Credalti is a credit repair company. The client tells us which items are wrong and why, and that statement is recorded with a date before any letter is prepared. Credalti then prepares each letter and mails it for the client, under the client's written authorization.

How the letters are sent is the point we most need your advice on: see the first item under "What we are asking you to check".

This packet shows each letter as it is in the software (version 1). The owner can change a letter's wording in the software's letter editor; every change is a new version that comes to you in a separate, shorter packet showing exactly what changed. The software mails a letter to a real client only after your approval of that exact text has been recorded, with your name and the date; until then, a round of letters that uses it is not sent.

### The rules these drafts were written to

The new drafts follow the rules below. The original letters were written before these rules and are reproduced unchanged; where an original departs from a rule, its note says so.

- First person, plain and polite English, the consumer's own voice.
- A letter states a fact only if the client has stated it. Each entry lists the "facts the client must have provided"; without them the letter may not be used.
- The law is cited for what is being asked and not overstated. In particular, FCRA § 609 is treated only as a right to see the file. No new letter says or implies that § 609, or a missing original contract, requires anything to be deleted.
- No threats, no demands for money, no accusations that the recipient broke the law. Follow-up letters may say the consumer may submit a complaint to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.
- No promises about results, to anyone.

### What we are asking you to check

- Whether letters that Credalti prepares and mails may go out in the client's name without saying so; what authorization the client must sign for that (for example a limited power of attorney); and whether any of these letters should disclose Credalti's role.
- Each citation and each description of what a statute provides. The citations were checked by web search against passages quoted from the U.S. Code, the FTC, the CFPB and the Federal Reserve; the official texts could not be opened directly from our build environment, so please treat every citation as unconfirmed until you have checked it.
- Whether each letter says only what the listed client facts support, and whether the listed facts are the right ones to require.
- Tone: whether anything reads as a threat, a demand, an accusation or a promise.
- The 17 letters carrying an "Attorney attention" note (no. 9, no. 10, no. 14, no. 15, no. 18, no. 24, no. 25, no. 26, no. 27, no. 29, no. 30, no. 32, no. 33, no. 34, no. 35, no. 37, no. 40). These include the settlement offer, the goodwill request, the cease-communication request, the identity-theft letters and the medical-collection dispute.
- The ten original letters. Their wording is unchanged because the software depends on them; where an original is firmer than the new drafts, or cites the law loosely, its note says so and asks whether it should be reworded or replaced.
- Direct disputes to furnishers: 12 C.F.R. § 1022.43(b)(2) lets a furnisher decline to investigate a direct dispute it reasonably believes was prepared by a credit repair organization. Please advise how that applies to letters a client prepares with our software.
- Anything state-specific. These drafts cite federal law only.

### How to read each entry

Each entry gives the letter's title, its key in the software, who it is sent to, when staff may use it, the facts the client must have provided, the statutes it relies on, any note for you or for staff, and then the full letter as it would be mailed.

The sample consumer, accounts, creditor and collector are fictional and the same throughout. The enclosure list under each signature shows the suggested enclosures; a real letter lists only what is actually attached. A paragraph in [square brackets] marks where the client's own words are inserted; when the client gives none, that paragraph is left out.

One more thing to know: the software has two features, both switched off, that would make letters look less alike: automatic rewording of the prose, and rotating print and handwriting-style fonts. While they are off, every letter is mailed exactly as approved, in one plain print font. They stay off unless you advise that they are appropriate.

Please mark each entry on its last line: "Attorney decision: ☐ approve ☐ approve with changes ☐ do not use — notes:"

## 1. General dispute of accounts

*Disputa general de cuentas*

- **Key:** `dispute_611_accounts`
- **Status:** Original letter, in use today (wording unchanged)
- **Group:** Bureau disputes, by reason
- **Sent to:** Credit bureau (Equifax, Experian or TransUnion)
- **Stage:** First dispute
- **When it is used:** The client disputes one or more accounts and no reason-specific letter fits better.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 611 (15 U.S.C. § 1681i)

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client has attested, for each listed account, that the information is inaccurate, incomplete, unverifiable or outdated.

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)

**Note to staff:** Original round-engine letter; wording unchanged. It gives no item-specific reason, and a dispute without specifics is easier for a bureau to treat as frivolous under § 611(a)(3). Prefer a reason-specific letter when the client has given a reason.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text
Elena Marisol Vargas
1420 Sample Street, Apt 3B
San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Equifax Information Services LLC
P.O. Box 740256
Atlanta, GA 30374-0256
Re: Dispute of inaccurate account information — FCRA Section 611

To Whom It May Concern:

I am exercising my right under Section 611 of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. § 1681i) to dispute the following accounts on my credit report. I believe each item listed below is inaccurate, unverifiable, or outdated:

- Northgate Bank (****4821 · charged off)

Please conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of each item, and delete or correct any information that cannot be verified as accurate and complete. Please send me written results of your reinvestigation and a free updated copy of my report if any change is made.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas

Enclosures:
- Copy of government-issued photo ID
- Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)
```

**Attorney decision: ☐ approve ☐ approve with changes ☐ do not use — notes:**

## 2. Dispute: account is not mine

*Disputa: la cuenta no es mía*

- **Key:** `bureau_not_my_account`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** Bureau disputes, by reason
- **Sent to:** Credit bureau (Equifax, Experian or TransUnion)
- **Stage:** First dispute
- **When it is used:** The client states they did not open the account or authorize anyone to open it, and is not claiming identity theft.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 611 (15 U.S.C. § 1681i)

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client states each listed account is not theirs: they did not open it and did not authorize anyone to open it in their name.
- Client confirms they are not a joint holder, co-signer or authorized user on the account.

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)

**Note to staff:** If the client says the account was opened by someone using their identity, use the identity-theft letters instead; this letter does not claim identity theft.

```text

P.O. Box 740256
Atlanta, GA 30374-0256

Please send me the written results of your reinvestigation.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas

## 3. Dispute: late payments reported in error

*Disputa: pagos atrasados reportados por error*

- **Key:** `bureau_never_late`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** Bureau disputes, by reason
- **Sent to:** Credit bureau (Equifax, Experian or TransUnion)
- **Stage:** First dispute
- **When it is used:** The report shows late payments on an account and the client states they paid on time.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 611 (15 U.S.C. § 1681i)

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client states the payments reported as late were made on time.

## 6. Dispute: duplicate account

*Disputa: cuenta duplicada*

- **Key:** `bureau_duplicate_account`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** Bureau disputes, by reason
- **Sent to:** Credit bureau (Equifax, Experian or TransUnion)
- **Stage:** First dispute
- **When it is used:** The same account appears more than once on the same bureau's report as if it were separate accounts.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 611 (15 U.S.C. § 1681i)

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client states the listed entries are one and the same account reported more than once.

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)

**Note to staff:** An original creditor's account and a collection agency's account for the same debt are normally two legitimate entries, not a duplicate. Use this letter only when the same creditor or the same collector reports the same account twice.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text
Elena Marisol Vargas
1420 Sample Street, Apt 3B
San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Equifax Information Services LLC
P.O. Box 740256
Atlanta, GA 30374-0256
Re: Dispute of account reported more than once — FCRA Section 611

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing to dispute the following entries on my credit report. They refer to one and the same account, but they are reported as if they were separate accounts, so the same debt is counted more than once:

- Northgate Bank (****4821 · charged off)

The specifics are as follows: [The client's own words appear here: what is wrong and what the correct information is, or the client's statement or offer.]

Under Section 611 of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. § 1681i), I ask that you conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of these entries, keep a single accurate entry for the account, and delete the duplicate reporting.

I have enclosed the documents listed at the end of this letter.

Please send me the written results of your reinvestigation.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas

Enclosures:
- Copy of government-issued photo ID
- Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)
```

## 9. Dispute: account discharged in bankruptcy still showing a balance

*Disputa: cuenta incluida en bancarrota que aún muestra saldo*

- **Key:** `bureau_included_in_bankruptcy`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** Bureau disputes, by reason
- **Sent to:** Credit bureau (Equifax, Experian or TransUnion)
- **Stage:** First dispute
- **When it is used:** The debt was included and discharged in the client's bankruptcy and the report still shows a balance or past-due amount.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 611 (15 U.S.C. § 1681i)

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client states they filed a bankruptcy case and received a discharge.
- Client states each listed debt was included in that bankruptcy case and discharged.
- Client provides the discharge order and, ideally, the schedule listing the creditor.

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement); Bankruptcy discharge order; Bankruptcy schedule listing the creditor

**Attorney attention:** The letter states that the listed debts were discharged. Not every debt listed in a bankruptcy is discharged (for example reaffirmed debts and debts excepted from discharge), and a case that is still open has no discharge yet. Please confirm what staff must check before using it.

## 10. Dispute: information past its reporting period

*Disputa: información fuera del período de reporte*

- **Key:** `bureau_obsolete_item`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** Bureau disputes, by reason
- **Sent to:** Credit bureau (Equifax, Experian or TransUnion)
- **Stage:** First dispute
- **When it is used:** By the client's records, the negative item is older than the period for which it may be reported.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 605 (15 U.S.C. § 1681c); FCRA § 605(c) (15 U.S.C. § 1681c(c)); FCRA § 611 (15 U.S.C. § 1681i)

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client states, with dates, when the delinquency began (or when the public record was entered), and that date puts the item past its reporting period.

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement); Statement or letter showing when the delinquency began

**Attorney attention:** The letter says § 605 limits most adverse information 'in most cases to seven years' and describes the § 605(c) starting point. It is not for bankruptcy cases, which have a longer period under § 605(a)(1), or for reports within the § 605(b) exceptions. Please confirm the wording and the periods staff should apply; we could not open the full text of § 605(a) to confirm every period.

**Note to staff:** Do not use for bankruptcy entries. Work out the date with the client; never estimate it.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text
Elena Marisol Vargas
1420 Sample Street, Apt 3B
San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Equifax Information Services LLC
P.O. Box 740256
Atlanta, GA 30374-0256
Re: Dispute of information past its reporting period — FCRA Sections 605 and 611

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing to dispute the following item(s) on my credit report. Based on my records, each one is older than the period for which it may be reported:

- Northgate Bank (****4821 · charged off)

The specifics are as follows: [The client's own words appear here: what is wrong and what the correct information is, or the client's statement or offer.]

Section 605 of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. § 1681c) limits how long most adverse information may appear in a consumer report, in most cases to seven years. For an account placed for collection or charged off, Section 605(c) measures that period from 180 days after the start of the delinquency that led to the collection or charge-off.

Under Section 611 of the Act (15 U.S.C. § 1681i), I ask that you conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of the dates reported for each item listed, including the date of first delinquency, and delete any item that is past its reporting period.

I have enclosed the documents listed at the end of this letter.

Please send me the written results of your reinvestigation.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas

Enclosures:
- Copy of government-issued photo ID
- Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)
- Statement or letter showing when the delinquency began
```

## 15. Request for description of the reinvestigation procedure (method of verification)

*Solicitud del procedimiento de reinvestigación (método de verificación)*

- **Key:** `mov_request`
- **Status:** Original letter, in use today (wording unchanged)
- **Group:** Bureau follow-ups
- **Sent to:** Credit bureau (Equifax, Experian or TransUnion)
- **Stage:** After the bureau says 'verified'
- **When it is used:** The bureau answered that the disputed item was 'verified' and the client wants to know how it was verified.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 611(a)(6)(B)(iii) (15 U.S.C. § 1681i(a)(6)(B)(iii)); FCRA § 611(a)(7) (15 U.S.C. § 1681i(a)(7))

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client previously disputed each listed item with this bureau and the bureau reported it as verified.

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement); Copy of the bureau's results or notice

**Attorney attention:** Original round-engine letter; wording unchanged. Two points: (1) it cites only § 611(a)(6)(B)(iii), which is the notice that a description is available; the duty to provide the description within 15 days of a request is § 611(a)(7). (2) Its last sentence asks for deletion 'if you cannot provide the method of verification'. The statute does not make deletion the consequence of not providing the description; please consider whether that sentence should be reworded.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text
Elena Marisol Vargas
1420 Sample Street, Apt 3B
San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Equifax Information Services LLC
P.O. Box 740256
Atlanta, GA 30374-0256
Re: Request for method of verification — FCRA Section 611(a)(6)(B)(iii)

To Whom It May Concern:

I previously disputed the items listed below and you reported them as "verified." Under FCRA Section 611(a)(6)(B)(iii), I am requesting a description of the procedure used to determine the accuracy and completeness of the disputed information, including the business name, address, and telephone number of each furnisher contacted:

- Northgate Bank (****4821 · charged off)

If you cannot provide the method of verification, or the items cannot in fact be verified, please delete them and send me an updated copy of my credit report.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas

Enclosures:
- Copy of government-issued photo ID
- Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)
- Copy of the bureau's results or notice
```

## 17. Follow-up: no response after the reinvestigation period

*Seguimiento: sin respuesta después del plazo de reinvestigación*

- **Key:** `bureau_no_response`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** Bureau follow-ups
- **Sent to:** Credit bureau (Equifax, Experian or TransUnion)
- **Stage:** Follow-up
- **When it is used:** More than 30 days have passed since the bureau received the dispute and the client has not received the results.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 611(a)(1) (15 U.S.C. § 1681i(a)(1)); FCRA § 611(a)(6) (15 U.S.C. § 1681i(a)(6))

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client mailed a written dispute of the listed items to this bureau.
- Proof of delivery shows the bureau received it more than 30 days ago.
- Client has not received results by mail or in the bureau's online account.

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement); Copy of the earlier dispute letter and proof of mailing or delivery

**Note to staff:** Count from the date the bureau received the dispute, and allow for mailing time of the results. The period can be 45 days when the client sent additional information during the 30 days (§ 611(a)(1)(B)) or disputed after a free annual report (§ 612(a)(3)); wait until that longer period has passed in those cases.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text
Elena Marisol Vargas
1420 Sample Street, Apt 3B
San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Equifax Information Services LLC
P.O. Box 740256
Atlanta, GA 30374-0256
Re: Follow-up: no results received for my dispute — FCRA Section 611

To Whom It May Concern:

I am following up on a written dispute I mailed to you about the item(s) listed below. More than 30 days have passed since you received it, and I have not received the results of your reinvestigation:

- Northgate Bank (****4821 · charged off)

For your reference: [The client's own words appear here: what is wrong and what the correct information is, or the client's statement or offer.]

Section 611(a)(1) of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. § 1681i) provides for a reinvestigation to be completed within 30 days after the agency receives the dispute, with a limited extension in some cases, and Section 611(a)(6) provides for written notice of the results within five business days after the reinvestigation is completed.

I ask that you complete the reinvestigation, send me the written results, and correct or delete any information that was not verified.

I have enclosed the documents listed at the end of this letter.

If this remains unresolved, I may ask the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau for help by submitting a complaint.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas

Enclosures:
- Copy of government-issued photo ID
- Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)
- Copy of the earlier dispute letter and proof of mailing or delivery
```

**Attorney decision: ☐ approve ☐ approve with changes ☐ do not use — notes:**

## 18. Response to a 'frivolous' determination, with added specifics

*Respuesta a una determinación de disputa «frívola», con datos adicionales*

- **Key:** `bureau_frivolous_response`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** Bureau follow-ups
- **Sent to:** Credit bureau (Equifax, Experian or TransUnion)
- **Stage:** Follow-up
- **When it is used:** The bureau gave notice that it will not investigate the dispute because it considers it frivolous or irrelevant, and the client can give more detail.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 611(a)(3) (15 U.S.C. § 1681i(a)(3)); FCRA § 611 (15 U.S.C. § 1681i)

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client received a notice from this bureau that the dispute was determined to be frivolous or irrelevant.
- Client states the dispute is their own and made in good faith.
- Client provides, in their own words, what is wrong with each item and any supporting documents (this is the letter's `details`).

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement); Copy of the bureau's results or notice; Documents supporting the dispute

**Attorney attention:** The letter says 'This dispute is mine, I am making it in good faith'. Bureaus often send frivolous notices when they suspect a credit repair company prepared the letter. Please confirm this sentence is accurate and appropriate given that the client reviews, approves and sends a letter drafted with our software.

**Note to staff:** Do not send without the client's own specifics. Repeating the same dispute with no new information invites the same answer.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text
Elena Marisol Vargas
1420 Sample Street, Apt 3B
San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Equifax Information Services LLC
P.O. Box 740256
Atlanta, GA 30374-0256
Re: Response to your notice about my dispute, with additional information — FCRA Section 611(a)(3)

To Whom It May Concern:

You notified me that you would not reinvestigate my dispute of the item(s) listed below because you considered it frivolous or irrelevant. This dispute is mine, I am making it in good faith, and I am writing to give you the information you need to investigate it:

- Northgate Bank (****4821 · charged off)

The specific information I dispute, and why, is as follows: [The client's own words appear here: what is wrong and what the correct information is, or the client's statement or offer.]

I have enclosed the documents listed at the end of this letter.

Section 611(a)(3) of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. § 1681i) provides that a notice of this kind give the reasons for the determination and identify any information required to investigate the disputed information. If you still need something more from me, please tell me exactly what it is.

With this additional information, I ask that you conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of each item listed under Section 611 and send me the written results.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas

Enclosures:
- Copy of government-issued photo ID
- Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)
- Copy of the bureau's results or notice
- Documents supporting the dispute
```

## 20. Deleted item reinserted without notice

*Partida eliminada que reapareció sin aviso*

- **Key:** `bureau_reinsertion_notice`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** Bureau follow-ups
- **Sent to:** Credit bureau (Equifax, Experian or TransUnion)
- **Stage:** Follow-up
- **When it is used:** An item the bureau deleted after a dispute is back on the report and the client received no written notice.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 611(a)(5)(B) (15 U.S.C. § 1681i(a)(5)(B)); FCRA § 611 (15 U.S.C. § 1681i)

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client disputed each listed item and the bureau's results show it was deleted.
- The same item appears again on a later report from the same bureau.
- Client did not receive a written notice of reinsertion from the bureau.

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement); Copy of the bureau's results showing the deletion; Page of the later report showing the item

**Note to staff:** Check that it is the same account from the same furnisher, not the same debt reported by a new collector, which is a new item.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text
Elena Marisol Vargas
1420 Sample Street, Apt 3B
San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Equifax Information Services LLC
P.O. Box 740256
Atlanta, GA 30374-0256
Re: Previously deleted information has reappeared — FCRA Section 611(a)(5)(B)

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing about the item(s) listed below. They were deleted from my credit file after I disputed them. They now appear on my credit report again, and I did not receive written notice from you that they had been put back:

- Northgate Bank (****4821 · charged off)

For your reference: [The client's own words appear here: what is wrong and what the correct information is, or the client's statement or offer.]

Section 611(a)(5)(B) of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. § 1681i) provides that information deleted after a reinvestigation may be reinserted only if the company that furnished it certifies that it is complete and accurate, and that the consumer be notified in writing within five business days after the reinsertion.

I ask that you send me that notice, including the name and address of the company that furnished the information and its telephone number if reasonably available. I also dispute the reinserted information under Section 611 and ask that you conduct a reasonable reinvestigation of it. If it cannot be verified as accurate and complete, please delete it.

I have enclosed the documents listed at the end of this letter.

Please send me the written results of your reinvestigation.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas

Enclosures:
- Copy of government-issued photo ID
- Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)
- Copy of the bureau's results showing the deletion
- Page of the later report showing the item
```

## 24. Direct dispute with the furnisher

*Disputa directa con el proveedor de datos*

- **Key:** `furnisher_direct`
- **Status:** Original letter, in use today (wording unchanged)
- **Group:** Creditor or furnisher
- **Sent to:** Creditor or other furnisher
- **Stage:** Direct to the furnisher
- **When it is used:** The client disputes the information directly with the company that reports it.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 623(a)(8) (15 U.S.C. § 1681s-2(a)(8)); 12 C.F.R. § 1022.43

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client has attested, for each listed item, that the information the furnisher reports is inaccurate.

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)

**Attorney attention:** Original round-engine letter; wording unchanged. It says 'you are required to' and 'you must correct it or cease reporting it', which is firmer than the new letters. The round engine also uses it for inquiries and public records; as we understand 12 C.F.R. § 1022.43(b)(1), the direct-dispute rule does not cover disputes about inquiries or public record information, so please confirm whether it should. 12 C.F.R. § 1022.43(b)(2), and the parallel exclusion in FCRA § 623(a)(8), say a furnisher need not investigate a direct dispute it reasonably believes was prepared by, or submitted on a form supplied by, a credit repair organization. Please advise how that affects direct-dispute letters prepared with our software and sent by the client.

**Note to staff:** Send to the address the furnisher gives for disputes (on the credit report or on its statements). A direct dispute should identify the account, say what is wrong and why, and include supporting documents.

```text

San Antonio, TX 78205

Attn: Credit Reporting Disputes
P.O. Box 2500
Wilmington, DE 19801

- Northgate Bank (****4821 · charged off)

Under FCRA Section 623(a)(8) and 12 C.F.R. § 1022.43, you are required to conduct a reasonable investigation of this direct dispute. If you cannot verify the disputed information as accurate and complete, you must correct it or cease reporting it to all consumer reporting agencies, and notify me of the outcome.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas

*Solicitud de corrección de la fecha de primera morosidad*

- **Key:** `furnisher_date_of_first_delinquency`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** Creditor or furnisher
- **Sent to:** Creditor or other furnisher
- **Stage:** Direct to the furnisher

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client states the date of first delinquency being reported is wrong.
- Client gives the date their records show and how they know it (this is the letter's `details`).

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement); Statement or letter showing when the delinquency began

**Attorney attention:** 12 C.F.R. § 1022.43(b)(2), and the parallel exclusion in FCRA § 623(a)(8), say a furnisher need not investigate a direct dispute it reasonably believes was prepared by, or submitted on a form supplied by, a credit repair organization. Please advise how that affects direct-dispute letters prepared with our software and sent by the client.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text
Elena Marisol Vargas
1420 Sample Street, Apt 3B
San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Northgate Bank
Attn: Credit Reporting Disputes
P.O. Box 2500
Wilmington, DE 19801
Re: Direct dispute of the date of first delinquency you report — FCRA Section 623

To Whom It May Concern:

The specifics are as follows: [The client's own words appear here: what is wrong and what the correct information is, or the client's statement or offer.]

Under Section 623(a)(8) and 12 C.F.R. § 1022.43, I ask that you conduct a reasonable investigation, check the date against the account records, correct the date of first delinquency with each consumer reporting agency to which you furnish this account, and send me the results.

It is written as an offer that asks, without demanding, that the furnisher update or delete its reporting, and says the decision is the furnisher's. Please say whether the company should offer this letter at all.

## 30. Debt validation request (original)

*Solicitud de validación de deuda (original)*

- **Key:** `debt_validation`
- **Status:** Original letter, in use today (wording unchanged)
- **Group:** Debt collector
- **Sent to:** Debt collector
- **Stage:** First dispute
- **When it is used:** A collection agency reports a debt and the client asks it to validate the debt; use it only within 30 days of the first notice.
- **Statutes:** FDCPA § 809(b) (15 U.S.C. § 1692g(b)); FCRA § 623(a)(3) (15 U.S.C. § 1681s-2(a)(3))

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client disputes the debt or wants it verified.
- Client received the collector's first notice less than 30 days ago.

**Suggested enclosures:** None

**Attorney attention:** Original round-engine letter; wording unchanged. Three points: (1) the letter does not say it is sent within 30 days of the collector's first notice, which is when § 809(b) applies; collector_validation_30_day is the replacement that does. (2) It asks for 'a copy of the original signed agreement', which § 809(b) does not expressly require as verification. (3) It asks the collector to delete its reporting if it cannot validate; § 809(b) pauses collection until verification and does not itself require deletion. Please say whether the round engine should switch to the new letter.

**Note to staff:** FDCPA § 809(b) applies only to a written dispute sent within 30 days after the client received the collector's first (validation) notice. Outside that window the collector has no duty under § 809(b) to verify or to pause collection; confirm the date with the client before using this letter.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text
Elena Marisol Vargas
1420 Sample Street, Apt 3B
San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Summit Recovery Services
P.O. Box 4400
Columbus, OH 43216
Re: Request for validation of debt — FDCPA Section 809(b)

To Whom It May Concern:

I am requesting validation of the debt(s) you claim I owe and which you report to consumer reporting agencies:

- Summit Recovery Services (****7730 · collection)

Under Section 809(b) of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (15 U.S.C. § 1692g), I request that you provide: (1) proof that you own this debt or are authorized to collect it; (2) a complete accounting of the amount claimed, including the original creditor's name and account number; and (3) a copy of the original signed agreement creating the obligation.

Until this debt is validated, please cease reporting it to any consumer reporting agency, or report it as disputed as required by FCRA Section 623(a)(3). If you cannot validate it, please delete your reporting of it and confirm to me in writing.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas
```

**Attorney decision: ☐ approve ☐ approve with changes ☐ do not use — notes:**

The letter states that it is sent within thirty days; do not use it if that is not true.

## 32. Follow-up: verification of debt not received

*Seguimiento: verificación de deuda no recibida*

- **Key:** `collector_validation_follow_up`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** Debt collector
- **Sent to:** Debt collector
- **Stage:** Follow-up
- **When it is used:** The client sent the verification request in time and the collection agency has not answered.
- **Statutes:** FDCPA § 809(b) (15 U.S.C. § 1692g(b))

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client sent a written dispute or verification request to this collector within 30 days of receiving its first notice, and has proof of mailing.
- Client has not received verification of the debt.

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of the earlier verification request and proof of mailing or delivery

**Attorney attention:** The letter asks, as a request, that a collector that cannot verify the debt close its file and ask the bureaus to delete its reporting. § 809(b) itself only pauses collection until verification is mailed; it sets no deadline and does not require deletion. Please confirm the request is worded modestly enough, and that the sentence about a CFPB complaint is acceptable here.

**Note to staff:** FDCPA § 809(b) applies only to a written dispute sent within 30 days after the client received the collector's first (validation) notice. Outside that window the collector has no duty under § 809(b) to verify or to pause collection; confirm the date with the client before using this letter. The statute sets no deadline for the collector to send verification; it may also simply stop collecting.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text

San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Summit Recovery Services
P.O. Box 4400
Columbus, OH 43216

- Summit Recovery Services (****7730 · collection)

For your reference: [The client's own words appear here: what is wrong and what the correct information is, or the client's statement or offer.]

Section 809(b) of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (15 U.S.C. § 1692g(b)) provides for a debt collector that receives a timely written dispute to stop collection of the debt until verification is mailed to the consumer.

I ask again that you send me verification of the debt and the name and address of the original creditor. If you are not able to verify the debt, please confirm in writing that you have closed your file, and ask each consumer reporting agency to which you reported the debt to delete your reporting of it.

I have enclosed the documents listed at the end of this letter.

If this remains unresolved, I may ask the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau for help by submitting a complaint.

This letter is not an acknowledgment that I owe this debt.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas

- **Sent to:** Debt collector
- **When it is used:** The client expressly asks that the collection agency stop contacting them and understands the consequences.
- **Statutes:** FDCPA § 805(c) (15 U.S.C. § 1692c(c))

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client states this collector has been contacting them about the listed debt.
- Client has explicitly asked for a cease-communication letter after being told that it does not erase the debt and that the collector or creditor may still take legal action.

**Suggested enclosures:** None

**Attorney attention:** A cease-communication letter does not erase the debt, does not stop credit reporting, and ends the informal contact through which a debt is often resolved; a collector that can no longer call or write may decide to file a lawsuit. § 805(c) binds debt collectors, not original creditors collecting their own debts. Please confirm the warning staff must give and whether the client's request should be recorded in writing.

**Note to staff:** Use only at the client's explicit request. It does not erase the debt and can lead to a lawsuit. Never suggest it as a way to improve credit.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text
Elena Marisol Vargas
1420 Sample Street, Apt 3B
San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Summit Recovery Services
P.O. Box 4400
Columbus, OH 43216
Re: Request to stop communication — FDCPA Section 805(c)

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing about the debt(s) listed below, about which you have been contacting me:

- Summit Recovery Services (****7730 · collection)

Under Section 805(c) of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (15 U.S.C. § 1692c(c)), I am notifying you in writing that I wish you to stop communicating with me about this debt.

I understand that the Act allows you to contact me to confirm that you are ending your collection efforts, or to tell me about a specific remedy you may or intend to use.

This letter is not an acknowledgment that I owe this debt.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas
```

## 34. Disputed debt reported while verification is outstanding

*Deuda disputada que aparece en el reporte mientras la verificación está pendiente*

- **Key:** `collector_dispute_while_validation_pending`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** Debt collector
- **Sent to:** Debt collector
- **Stage:** Follow-up
- **When it is used:** The client asked for verification in time, has not received it, and the collection appears on their credit report.
- **Statutes:** FDCPA § 809(b) (15 U.S.C. § 1692g(b)); FCRA § 623(a)(3) (15 U.S.C. § 1681s-2(a)(3))

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client sent a written dispute or verification request to this collector within 30 days of receiving its first notice, and has proof of mailing.
- Client has not received verification of the debt.
- The collection appears on the client's current credit report.

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of the earlier verification request and proof of mailing or delivery

**Attorney attention:** The letter does not say that reporting a debt while verification is outstanding is unlawful, because whether credit reporting is collection activity that § 809(b) pauses is not settled. It asks for verification, for the debt to be reported as disputed (§ 623(a)(3)), and for correction or deletion if the collector's records do not support it. Please confirm that framing.

**Note to staff:** FDCPA § 809(b) applies only to a written dispute sent within 30 days after the client received the collector's first (validation) notice. Outside that window the collector has no duty under § 809(b) to verify or to pause collection; confirm the date with the client before using this letter.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text
Elena Marisol Vargas
1420 Sample Street, Apt 3B
San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Summit Recovery Services
P.O. Box 4400
Columbus, OH 43216
Re: Disputed debt appearing on my credit report while verification is outstanding — FDCPA Section 809(b)

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing about the debt(s) listed below. I sent you a written dispute and request for verification within thirty days of receiving your first notice about the debt. I have not received verification, and the debt appears on my credit report:

- Summit Recovery Services (****7730 · collection)

For your reference: [The client's own words appear here: what is wrong and what the correct information is, or the client's statement or offer.]

I continue to dispute this debt. I ask that you: (1) send me the verification described in Section 809(b) of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (15 U.S.C. § 1692g(b)); (2) report the debt as disputed to each consumer reporting agency to which you furnish it, as Section 623(a)(3) of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. § 1681s-2) provides for information a consumer has disputed with the furnisher; and (3) correct or delete your reporting if your records do not support it.

I have enclosed the documents listed at the end of this letter.

Please confirm in writing what you have done.

This letter is not an acknowledgment that I owe this debt.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas

Enclosures:
- Copy of the earlier verification request and proof of mailing or delivery
```

## 35. Identity theft block

*Bloqueo de información por robo de identidad*

- **Key:** `identity_theft_block`
- **Status:** Original letter, in use today (wording unchanged)
- **Group:** Identity theft
- **Sent to:** Credit bureau (Equifax, Experian or TransUnion)
- **Stage:** First dispute
- **When it is used:** The client is a victim of identity theft, has an identity theft report, and asks the bureau to block the resulting items.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 605B (15 U.S.C. § 1681c-2)

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client states they are a victim of identity theft.
- Client states each listed item resulted from identity theft: a transaction they did not make or authorize.
- Client has filed an identity theft report (FTC IdentityTheft.gov report or police report) and provides a copy.

**Suggested enclosures:** Identity theft report (FTC); Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)

**Attorney attention:** Original round-engine letter; wording unchanged. It states as fact that the client is a victim of identity theft and that an identity theft report is enclosed. An untrue identity theft claim has serious consequences for the client, and a bureau may decline or rescind a block it believes was requested in error or by misrepresentation. The existing wording also says 'you must block ... within four (4) business days', which is firmer than the new letters. Please confirm the safeguards: staff never suggest this letter, and it is sent only with the client's own statement and report.

**Note to staff:** Never suggest identity theft to a client. Do not send unless the identity theft report is physically enclosed.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text
Elena Marisol Vargas
1420 Sample Street, Apt 3B
San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Equifax Information Services LLC
P.O. Box 740256
Atlanta, GA 30374-0256
Re: Request to block information resulting from identity theft — FCRA Section 605B

To Whom It May Concern:

I am a victim of identity theft. The following items on my credit report resulted from transactions I did not make or authorize:

- Northgate Bank (****4821 · charged off)

Under FCRA Section 605B (15 U.S.C. § 1681c-2), you must block the reporting of this information within four (4) business days of receiving this request. Enclosed are a copy of my identity theft report and proof of my identity.

Please confirm the block in writing and notify the furnishers of this information as required by law.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas

Enclosures:
- Identity theft report (FTC)
- Copy of government-issued photo ID
- Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)
```

**Attorney decision: ☐ approve ☐ approve with changes ☐ do not use — notes:**

## 36. Request for an initial fraud alert

*Solicitud de alerta de fraude inicial*

- **Key:** `identity_fraud_alert`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** Identity theft
- **Sent to:** Credit bureau (Equifax, Experian or TransUnion)
- **When it is used:** The client suspects in good faith that they have been or are about to become a victim of fraud or identity theft and wants an alert on their file.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 605A(a) (15 U.S.C. § 1681c-1(a))

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client states they suspect in good faith that they have been, or are about to become, a victim of fraud or identity theft.
- Client asks for a fraud alert and understands lenders may take extra steps to confirm their identity while it is in place.

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)

**Note to staff:** One nationwide bureau refers an initial alert to the other two, so one letter is enough. Fraud alerts are normally requested online or by phone, and the dispute address may not be the bureau's fraud-alert address; check the address before mailing. An extended alert is a separate request that requires an identity theft report.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text
Elena Marisol Vargas
1420 Sample Street, Apt 3B
San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Equifax Information Services LLC
P.O. Box 740256
Atlanta, GA 30374-0256
Re: Request for an initial fraud alert — FCRA Section 605A

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing to ask that you place an initial fraud alert on my credit file. I suspect in good faith that I have been, or am about to become, a victim of fraud or identity theft.

Section 605A(a) of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. § 1681c-1) provides for an initial fraud alert to be placed in a consumer's file for at least one year at the consumer's request, and for the request to be referred to the other nationwide consumer reporting agencies.

I have enclosed the documents listed at the end of this letter.

Please confirm in writing that the alert has been placed, and tell me how to request the free copy of my file that is available with a fraud alert.

If you need anything further to identify me, please let me know.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas

Enclosures:
- Copy of government-issued photo ID
- Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)
```

**Attorney decision: ☐ approve ☐ approve with changes ☐ do not use — notes:**

## 37. Identity theft notice to the furnisher

*Aviso de robo de identidad al proveedor de datos*

- **Key:** `identity_theft_furnisher_notice`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** Identity theft
- **Sent to:** Creditor or other furnisher
- **Stage:** Direct to the furnisher
- **When it is used:** The client is a victim of identity theft and asks the company reporting the debt to stop reporting it, enclosing their FTC report.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 623(a)(6) (15 U.S.C. § 1681s-2(a)(6))

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client states they are a victim of identity theft.
- Client states each listed account or debt resulted from identity theft: they did not open, use or authorize it.
- Client has filed an identity theft report (FTC IdentityTheft.gov report or police report) and provides a copy to enclose.

**Suggested enclosures:** Identity theft report (FTC); Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)

**Attorney attention:** States as fact that the client is a victim of identity theft and that the identity theft report is enclosed; the same safeguards as the § 605B block apply. § 623(a)(6)(B) applies when the report is sent to the address the furnisher specifies for identity theft reports, so the letter asks for the correct address if this is not it. Please confirm the paraphrase of § 623(a)(6)(B).

**Note to staff:** Never suggest identity theft to a client. Do not send unless the identity theft report is physically enclosed.

**The letter (sample data):**

```text
Elena Marisol Vargas
1420 Sample Street, Apt 3B
San Antonio, TX 78205

January 15, 2026

Northgate Bank
Attn: Credit Reporting Disputes
P.O. Box 2500
Wilmington, DE 19801
Re: Notice of identity theft and request to stop reporting — FCRA Section 623(a)(6)

To Whom It May Concern:

I am a victim of identity theft. The following account(s) or debt(s), which you report in my name, resulted from identity theft. I did not open them, I did not use them, and I did not authorize them:

- Northgate Bank (****4821 · charged off)

I have enclosed a copy of my identity theft report and proof of my identity.

Section 623(a)(6)(B) of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. § 1681s-2) provides that when a consumer submits an identity theft report to a furnisher at the address the furnisher specifies for such reports, the furnisher may not furnish the information to any consumer reporting agency unless it later knows, or is informed by the consumer, that the information is correct.

I ask that you stop reporting this information to the consumer reporting agencies, ask them to delete what you have already reported, and close the account(s). If this is not the address you use for identity theft reports, please tell me the correct one.

Please confirm in writing what you have done.

Sincerely,

Elena Marisol Vargas

Enclosures:
- Identity theft report (FTC)
- Copy of government-issued photo ID
- Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)
```

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement); Copy of Social Security card

**Note to staff:** § 609 is a right to see the file, not a way to have anything taken off it, and it does not entitle the client to a creditor's original contract. A fee may apply unless a free disclosure is available; for the free ones use the § 612 letters or annualcreditreport.com.

I have enclosed the documents listed at the end of this letter.

## 40. Request for the free annual disclosure

*Solicitud de la divulgación anual gratuita*

- **Key:** `free_annual_disclosure_612`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** File and access
- **Sent to:** Secondary or specialty reporting agency
- **When it is used:** The client has not had their free annual disclosure from a specialty reporting agency in the last 12 months.
- **Statutes:** FCRA § 612(a) (15 U.S.C. § 1681j(a)); FCRA § 609 (15 U.S.C. § 1681g)

**Facts the client must have provided:**

- Client asks for their free annual file disclosure from this agency.
- Client states they have not received a free annual disclosure from this agency in the past 12 months.

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)

**Attorney attention:** § 612(a) free annual disclosures from Equifax, Experian and TransUnion must be requested through the centralized source (annualcreditreport.com or the Annual Credit Report Request Service), so this letter is meant for nationwide specialty agencies, which may require their own toll-free number or form. Please confirm a mailed letter is an acceptable way to ask, and that § 612(a) covers the agencies we send it to.

**Note to staff:** Not for Equifax, Experian or TransUnion: their free annual reports come only through annualcreditreport.com or the Annual Credit Report Request Service.

P.O. Box 1000
Atlanta, GA 30301

Please send the disclosure described in Section 609 of the Act (15 U.S.C. § 1681g) to me at the address above.

I have enclosed the documents listed at the end of this letter.

If you require this request to be made in another way, such as through a toll-free number or a request form, please tell me how.

Elena Marisol Vargas

## 42. Prescreen opt-out

*Exclusión de las listas de ofertas preaprobadas*

- **Key:** `prescreen_opt_out`
- **Status:** New draft, not in use
- **Group:** File and access
- **Sent to:** Credit bureau (Equifax, Experian or TransUnion)
- **When it is used:** The client wants to stop receiving prescreened offers of credit or insurance based on their file.

**Suggested enclosures:** Copy of government-issued photo ID; Proof of address (utility bill / bank statement)

**Note to staff:** The bureaus run a joint opt-out system (optoutprescreen.com, 1-888-5-OPT-OUT), which is the usual and faster way. An opt-out made there lasts five years; a permanent one needs the bureaus' signed form, which this letter asks for.

I would like this election to stay in effect until I tell you otherwise. If you require a signed notice of election form for that, please send it to me at the address above.

I have enclosed the documents listed at the end of this letter.

Please confirm in writing that my election has been recorded.

If you need anything further to identify me, please let me know.
